reading.body:
AutoGPT alone accounts for more than half of the 332,059 combined stars across these four autonomous-agent repositories, which means developer attention in this space is heavily concentrated in a single project rather than spread evenly across the field.

Three of the four repositories carry MIT licences, making their code freely reusable without negotiation. AutoGPT uses a custom licence, which matters because it is also the most-starred by a wide margin: developers building on the most popular foundation face licence terms that are not standardised. For AI specifically, the agent layer sits above the model and infrastructure layers, so licence constraints here propagate into whatever compute pipeline an agent eventually drives.

One repository, gpt-engineer, is archived. Its description explicitly names itself a precursor to a commercial product, which is a visible example of open exploration collapsing into a proprietary offering. The remaining three are actively pushed as recently as the data generation date. What this data does not cover is runtime compute demand, inference cost per agent loop, or how agent workloads translate into sustained power draw, so no conclusions about grid or building constraints can be drawn from it directly.
